newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban speaks of U.N. "disloyalty" to Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban speaks of U.N. "disloyalty" to Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban government said on Saturday it would be "disloyal" of the United Nations if the world body failed to recognise the Islamic movement's administration in Kabul.
A General Assembly committee on Friday deferred a decision on the credentials of Afghanistan's U.N. delegation, leaving in place representatives of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani.
The Taleban's acting information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told Reuters that his administration, which took power two weeks ago from Rabbani, deserved the U.N. seat.

"It will be disloyalty of the U.N. towards the Moslem nation of Afghanistan (if it does not recognise the Taleban). The present Islamic government represents the Afghan people who deserve to be recognised by the world," he said.

Hans Corell, U.N. legal counsel under-secretary, said in New York the committee had received several letters apparently sent by the Taleban demanding removal of Rabbani's delegation and saying the seat must be reserved "for the new ruling government".
The United States had proposed deferring a decision, while the Netherlands, backed by Russia, suggested an immediate decision to accept Rabanni's credentials.
No date was set for the next meeting of the U.N. committee.

Rabbani earlier this week was in northern provinces held by militia leader Abdul Rashid Dostum when Dostum signed a defensive alliance with another regional chief Kharim Khalili and Rabbani's former defence chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
Mutaqi said the Taleban movement, facing military reverses on its lines north of the capital Kabul, would continue to try to establish contacts with the United Nations.

"We (will) try to solve this issue through negotiations with the U.N. We try to establish contacts with them (U.N.) and if the talks fail or did not bear fruit then the acting council of Afghanistan will decide what to do," he said without elaborating.
